West Triangle, Quezon City http. liwww. dilg.gov.ph 1 8 JUN 2019 on-G OPINION NO. MAYOR CONSTANTINO H. REYES Municipal Mayor Municipality of Ubay Province of Bohol Dear Mayor Reyes: This has reference to your letter dated 6 March 2018 requesting this Department's legal opinion on the issues concerning the appointments made by the Acting Vice-Mayor (VM) and the incumbent VM. Per your letter, on 31 May 2017, then Acting VM Joan Abad-Balduman issued Job Order (JO) for several persons directing them to report for work as casual employees at the Office of the Sangguniang Bayan (SB) effective June 1-31, 2017. Likewise, on 29 November and 29 December 2017, the incumbent VM Nelson L. Uy similarly issued JOS and directed those persons included in the order to report for work as casual employees at the Office of the SB effective January 1-31, 2018. However, according to you, the JOS issued by the said Acting VM and VM reveal that they were directed to report for work as casual employees not only in the Office of the SB but also to the other offices that are under the authority and supervision of the Office of the Municipal Mayor. Thus, you alleged that the order by the Acting VM and VM have adversely affected your authority to appoint and determine suitable individuals to work under your office. On that account, you posed the following queries which we quote, in toto: i. ii. May an acting Municipal Vice-Mayor or the Municipal Vice-Mayor appoint casual employees to actually perform works at offices under the direct supervision and authority of the Office of the Municipal mayor without the latter's consent? Will the act of the acting Municipal Vice-Mayor or the Municipal Vice- Mayor in appointing casual employees to actually perform works at offices under the direct control and supervision of the Office of the Municipal Mayor violate the provisions of the Local Government Code or any existing laws, rules or regulations, particularly on separation of powers?

ii. Will the act Of the acting Municipal Vice-Mayor or the Municipal Vice- Mayor in appointing casual employees to actually perform works at offices under the direct control and supervision of the Office of the Municipal Mayor encroach upon, usurp, the authority of the Office of the Municipal Mayor to appoint casual employees for offices under its supervision? Foremost, you mentioned in your letter that there is an acting VM, hence, we presumed that there is temporary vacancy in the office of the VM only but not with respect to the Office of the Mayor. In Section 46 of the Local Government Code (LGC), there is temporary vacancy when the official is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons, such as, but not limited to: (1) leave of absence; (2) travel abroad; and (3) suspension from office. Since there is temporary vacancy in the office of the VM, the scope Of the acting VM's power necessarily includes the power to appoint, suspend or dismiss all officials and employees of the Sangguniang Bayan. This is only applicable if the vacancy exceeds thirty (30) days. Meanwhile, the Mayor has control and supervision over all the offices of the local government unit (LGU) except the Sangguniang Bayan. It follows then that the employees that should be assigned and/or appointed to said offices in the LGU should be decided by the Mayor. Moreover, as clearly pointed out in Section 444(b)(v), municipal mayor shall appoint all officials and employees whose salaries and wages are wholly or mainly paid out of municipal funds and whose appointments are not otherwise provided for in this Code, as well as those he may authorized by law to appoint. On the other hand, Section 445(a)(2) provides that the VM shall, subject to civil service law, rules and regulations, appoint all officials and employees of the Sangguniang Bayan, except those whose manner of appointment is specifically provided in the LGC. Hence, the duties and responsibilities of such employees should only be limited to the Office of the Sangguniang Bayan only. Relative to this, please be apprised that the above-mentioned queries have been settled by this Department in its DILG Legal Opinion No. 25, S.2016 dated 9 December 2016, where we opined that if the salaries of contractual/JO employees are derived from the appropriation of the Sanggunian, the City/Municipal Vice-Mayor or Vice-Governor, as the case may be, has the authority to appoint and accordingly assign them. In the said legal opinion, we upheld the Supreme Court's (SC) decision in the case of Atienza vs. Villarosal, where the SC held that: G.R. No. 161081, IOMay2005,

" (Underscoring supplied) In your letter, the duration and the reason of the temporary incapacity of the incumbent VM was not specified. Hence, we are of the assumption that the duration, as well as the reason of the temporary incapacity of the incumbent VM falls within the restrictions of the above-mentioned provision of the LGC. Accordingly, the following are the instances where employees are under the direct supervision and control of the mayor: (1) if the source of salaries and wages of the JOS appointed by the Acting VM and incumbent VM are wholly or mainly paid out of municipal funds; and (2) even if the source of fund of the employees is from the Office of the Sanggunian but assigned to other office/s other than the sanggunian. The power of the VM is limited to assigning or hiring of JOS only for the SB. Assigning them to other offices is an encroachment on the power of the LCE. This clearly constituted an encroachment on the appointment power of the mayor under Section 444(b)(1)(v)2 of RA No. 7160 or the Local Government Code (LGC) as the power of the VM to appoint is limited only to the Office of the Sanggunian (Section 445(a)(2)). z SECTION. 444.
